name: Thermal Dump Radiator Fins
description: Enlarges and vascularizes the ears using elephant ear thermoregulation genes, creating efficient biological radiators. The enlarged ears — approximately 1.5 times normal size — are densely threaded with blood vessels that dilate during exertion, flushing the ears with warm blood and radiating excess heat rapidly. The modification dramatically improves heat dissipation during intense physical activity, allowing the user to sustain peak performance in conditions that would cause heat exhaustion in an unmodified human. The ears visibly flush red during exertion and can be warm to the touch. Combined with arctic thermoregulation for cold resistance or fast-twitch muscle mods for sprint performance, the radiator ears prevent the overheating that limits maximum exertion. The larger ears also provide mildly enhanced hearing as a secondary benefit.
source_organism: Loxodonta africana (African elephant, vascular ear thermoregulation), Lepus californicus (black-tailed jackrabbit, ear radiator genes)
procedure: Auricular cartilage and vascular retroviral modification, 2 sessions
expression_time: 4–8 weeks for ear enlargement and vascularization
reversibility: Partially reversible; ear size can be reduced but vascular changes persist
side_effects: Ears are noticeably larger — not dramatically, but identifiably
Ears flush bright red during exercise, embarrassment, or heat
Ears are cold-sensitive — the increased surface area and thin skin lose heat rapidly in cold environments
Enhanced blood flow creates audible pulse sound in the ears during exertion
social_perception: Practical and mildly distinctive. Slightly larger, vascular ears are recognizable but not dramatic. The bright red flush during exertion is the most visible tell. In athletic communities, the modification is standard. Some users combine it with elf-ear elongation for a dual-purpose aesthetic-functional modification.
story_hooks: A Cooldown Mod user's ear vasculature is so enhanced that their ear temperature pattern is readable by thermal imaging at distance — a biometric identifier they can't suppress during exercise

A sprinter with radiator ears discovers their heat dissipation is so efficient that they can sustain fast-twitch performance 50% longer than expected — the combination of speed and endurance shouldn't be possible, and their competitors are suspicious
